datasets.title: Mudslide / Lahar impact in Sungai Pua and Banuhampu, Agam Metropolitan, Indonesia as of 20 May 2024
datasets.description: UNOSAT code: LS20240512IDN, GDACS ID: 1102617 This map illustrates satellite-detected mudslide / lahar in Sungai Pua and Banuhampu, Agam Metropolitan, Sumatera Barat Province, Indonesia, as observed from a Pléiades image acquired on 20 May 2024. Within the analyzed area of about 1,000 ha about 200 ha mudslide / lahar extent was observed. Based on Worldpop population data ~ 5,000 people within the analysed areas. Furthermore, within the analyzed area, 85 buildings are identified as affected by the floods (1% of the total structures in the analysed area), along with about 400 m of roads, as of 20 May 2024 This is a preliminary analysis and has not yet been validated in the field. Please send ground feedback to the United Nations Satellite Centre (UNOSAT).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/mudslide-lahar-impact-in-sungai-pua-and-banuhampu-agam-metropolitan-indonesia-as-of-20-may]
datasets.details: This is a preliminary assessment and has not yet been validated in the field. It is important to consider the characteristics of the source imagery used in the analyses when interpreting results. For damage assessments it should be noted that only significant damage to the structural integrity of the buildings analyzed can be seen in imagery, while minor damage such as cracks or holes may not be visible at all. For flood extractions using radar data it is important to note that urban areas and highly vegetated areas may mask the flood signature and result in underestimation of flood waters. Users with specific questions or concerns should contact unosat@unitar.org to seek clarification.

lineage.description: UNOSAT analysts interpreted Pléiades satellite imagery acquired on 20 May 2024 to detect and map mudslide/lahar extent in the Agam Metropolitan area. The 200 ha mudslide/lahar extent was delineated through visual change detection analysis. Exposure data from WorldPop was overlaid to estimate affected population (~5,000 people), and building footprints were identified and assessed for damage (85 affected structures).
